title: Self-Esteem Assessment
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: No learner rates another. Use story characters for low, healthy and inflated self-esteem.

skills.key_step: The child says what self-esteem is and tells healthy, low and inflated self-esteem by their signs and effects.

floor.question: Give a healthy way to manage sadness.

representations: a scale from low to inflated
steps: Name the effect on daily life.
Say how to build healthy self-esteem.
contexts: a learner who gives up after one mistake
a learner who boasts and looks down on others
a learner who tries again after failing

board.do: Draw a line with low, healthy and inflated.

board.say: A boy says he is better than everyone. Where does he go?

misconceptions.repair: Ask: can a person be confident and still kind?

misconceptions.ask: What can low self-esteem lead to?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how a child who thinks they cannot do anything behaves.

misconceptions.ask: A boy brags that he is better than everyone. What is this?
Achieng did badly in one test. Must her self-esteem be low?
misconceptions.repair: List other things Achieng does well.

checks.question: What is self-esteem?
checks.answer: how you value and respect yourself

checks.question: Give one effect of low self-esteem.
checks.answer: any of: giving up easily, withdrawing, being easily bullied
